findings.summary: DRATChecker.check and check_step skip _validate_steps: a negative literal gets ok=True on a satisfiable formula, the 0.1.7 hole, still open on the public streaming API (Python only)
deleting a reason clause leaves its root assignment in place: d -1 2 0, -2 0, 0 gets ok=True on the satisfiable (1)(-1 2), both engines, every shape
failed_clause keeps repeated literals on engine=native and drops them on engine=python
the variable bound in check_proof depends on the shape and on the text's length: 5 0 on a 2-variable formula is a verdict as text and ValueError as a list or MemoryProof, and 7 0 flips with a comment

check on a used checker (Python and Rust; the only way to read a Rust stream's result) reports ok=True, reached_empty=True and 'input formula is refuted' on a proof with no empty clause, and 'every step verified' after a rejected step
ProofWriter and MemoryProof.to_text turn a negative literal into a different clause, where check_proof on the same MemoryProof raises
_validate_steps lets a step's literals be a set: engine=python raises TypeError at the RAT check, engine=native returns a verdict

not_checked: cdclkit's own use of these APIs, and any proof a real solver wrote: proofs here are generated, tiny, and judged by the oracle
a Python binding for Rust Checker::check_step: none exists, so the crate is compiled and driven directly from a Rust driver embedded in this file

huge literals on the unguarded paths: DRATChecker and Rust Checker size their arrays for whatever literal they get, and Rust's docs say so. Only 40 variables past the formula were run, so the allocation itself was read, not exercised
a ProofWriter closed late or never: only properly closed writers are compared
re-using a checker after a rejected step beyond one more check([]) and two pieces

the text grammar itself (parsing corner), and deletion semantics past the first deleted reason: there only ok=True on a satisfiable formula and sat-preservation of accepted steps are judged, not exact counts
